concentration_flags: UBER is ~70.88% of NAV -- a single adverse event (the pending $40M California wrongful-death ruling, a broader rideshare-safety litigation wave, the pending Delivery Hero acquisition's integration/financing risk, execution/leverage risk from the EUR4.5B euro bond raise, or intensifying robotaxi competition from Tesla's Cybercab rollout, Wayve/London and Uber's own $10B robotaxi commitment) would disproportionately hit the portfolio; cash fell to ~10.62% of NAV this cycle (two new starter positions -- NVO and CHWY -- were funded from the cash buffer via queued trades), so the offsetting cushion against a UBER-specific shock is now thinner than in prior cycles.

trim_considerations.note: Bringing this back to the ~25% single-name guideline would mean reducing exposure by roughly $418.48 -- a consideration, not an instruction, and one that doesn't account for any tax consequences of selling, which this pipeline has no visibility into.
